explanation: Kinematics are physical: W=1.7 GeV is well above the eta-production threshold on the proton (m_p+m_eta ~ 1.486 GeV), Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0, and phi*=90 deg are all within the code's normal domain, so the point itself is generated as requested with model=maid2000 (3), ivec=1 (recoil proton), bmom=6.53 GeV (CLAS12 default), and vcut set to the requested -0.1. However, the documentation shipped with this repo (input.dat, examples/README.md, README.md) describes negative vcut as switching the cut from v^2 to a direct cut on v, but the actual Fortran source does not implement that: in exclurad.F, subroutine bornkin only applies the cut via 'if(cutv.gt.1d-12) vmax=min(vmax,cutv)' (exclurad.F:254). Any cutv <= 1e-12 -- including -0.1 -- fails that test, so vmax is left at its full kinematically-allowed maximum and no inelasticity cut is applied at all. In other words, running with vcut=-0.1 will behave identically to vcut=0 (no cut), not the documented 'cut on v' mode. The input file has been generated with vcut=-0.1 exactly as requested so the physicist can reproduce this behavior, but they should be aware the run will not actually restrict the radiated-photon phase space; if a genuine cut on v (rather than v^2) is needed, the source code's bornkin subroutine would need to be modified, since no such branch currently exists.
